data.title: TORC1 and PKA activity towards ribosome biogenesis oscillates in synchrony with the budding yeast cell cycle
data.authors: Guerra P; Milias-Argeitis A et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Budding yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae), time-lapse single-cell microscopy
data.finding: Tracking the localisation of two TORC1 and PKA targets by time-lapse microscopy in hundreds of yeast cells shows that TORC1/PKA activity towards ribosome biogenesis rises and falls in step with the cell cycle even when outside conditions stay constant; mutations in upstream regulators suggest internal metabolic signals partly drive the oscillation.
data.abstract_excerpt: Recent studies have revealed that the growth rate of budding yeast and mammalian cells varies during the cell cycle. By linking a multitude of signals to cell growth, the highly conserved target of rapamycin complex 1 (TORC1) and protein kinase A (PKA) pathways are prime candidates for mediating the dynamic coupling between growth and division. However, measurements of TORC1 and PKA activity during the cell cycle are still lacking.

extracted_findings.effect: TORC1/PKA output to ribosome biogenesis oscillates with the yeast cell cycle under constant conditions
